4e1151ef2d5fe10c.title: Dicarbon 100 Tablet
4e1151ef2d5fe10c.efficacy: An over-the-counter medicine used for supplementation of vitamin D during pregnancy/lactation, growth periods, and old age, and for prevention of poor bone and tooth development and rickets.
4e1151ef2d5fe10c.usage:
Children aged 8 and older and adults: take 1 tablet once daily.
Follow the prescribed dosage.
4e1151ef2d5fe10c.caution:
Do not take this medicine if any of the following applies: those hypersensitive to this medicine; infants under 12 months; hypercalcemia (excess calcium in the blood); sarcoidosis (a systemic inflammatory disease of unknown cause); kidney disease; kidney stones; severe renal failure; or hereditary problems such as galactose intolerance, Lapp lactase deficiency, or glucose-galactose malabsorption.

Consult a pharmacist before use if you are an infant under 1 year; a child who gets much sunlight and eats normally; are pregnant, may be pregnant, or are breastfeeding; premature infants, infants; cardiac/circulatory dysfunction; renal impairment; hypoproteinemia; or a history of kidney stones. If there is no improvement after about a month of use, stop immediately and consult a pharmacist.

Follow the prescribed dosage and usage.

When administering to children, do so under the guidance and supervision of a guardian.

Do not take with phosphates, calcium salts, oral tetracyclines, or antacids. Consult a pharmacist when taking with cardiac glycosides, antialdosterone agents, or triamterene. Avoid tannin-containing teas such as green tea and black tea during, before, and after taking this medicine.

If nausea, vomiting, diarrhea, constipation, low blood pressure, facial flushing, irregular heartbeat, or skin rash occur, stop immediately and consult a pharmacist.

summaryTable.How it works: Supplies vitamin D for pregnancy/lactation, growth and old age
summaryTable.Main symptoms: Vitamin D deficiency, poor bone/tooth development, rickets

4fc096b175507a1d.title: Almitin Plus Tablet
4fc096b175507a1d.efficacy: An over-the-counter medicine used for hyperacidity, heartburn, gastric discomfort, gastric bloating, indigestion (food stagnation), nausea, vomiting, stomach pain, and acid belching.
4fc096b175507a1d.usage:
Adults: take 1 tablet 3 times daily.
Follow the prescribed dosage.
4fc096b175507a1d.caution:
Do not take this medicine if any of the following applies: those hypersensitive to this medicine; those receiving dialysis therapy; hypermagnesemia; hyperphosphatemia; constipation; intestinal stenosis; acute appendicitis; women within the first 3 months of pregnancy; or children under 7 years.

Consult a pharmacist before use if you are pregnant, may be pregnant, or are breastfeeding; have hypermagnesemia or a history of magnesium deficiency; or have renal impairment or a history of kidney disease. If there is no improvement after about 2 weeks of use, stop immediately and consult a pharmacist.

Follow the prescribed dosage and usage.

Do not take with tetracycline antibiotics. Consult a pharmacist when taking with digoxin, captopril, cimetidine, ranitidine, famotidine, theophylline, propranolol, atenolol, ferrous sulfate, chlorpromazine, acetylsalicylic acid, naproxen, metoprolol, levodopa, ciprofloxacin, ofloxacin, chenodeoxycholic acid, sodium fluoride, isoniazid, enoxacin, norfloxacin, levothyroxine, coumarin derivatives, iron, or carbonated drinks. After taking an aluminum-containing antacid, avoid taking other medicines within 1–2 hours.

If diarrhea, constipation, abdominal bloating, skin rash, numbness, phosphate deficiency, or rarely headache, drowsiness, dizziness, or weakness occur, stop immediately and consult a pharmacist.

summaryTable.How it works: Antacid relieving hyperacidity and indigestion-related upper-abdominal symptoms
summaryTable.Main symptoms: Hyperacidity, heartburn, gastric discomfort/bloating, nausea, acid belching

5006d5f6f18fdf9b.usage:

Follow the prescribed dosage.
5006d5f6f18fdf9b.caution:
Follow the prescribed dosage and usage.

When administering to children, do so under the guidance and supervision of a guardian.

If, rarely, diarrhea, dry mouth, mild abdominal pain, rash, nausea, or vomiting occur, stop using immediately and consult a pharmacist.

summaryTable.How it works: Supplies vitamin C for skin conditions and pigmentation
summaryTable.Main symptoms: Eczema, acne, hives, skin rash, melasma, freckles, drug-induced dermatitis

576a17b04fc3ca8f.title: Aronamin Silver Premium Tablet
576a17b04fc3ca8f.efficacy: An over-the-counter medicine used for supplementation of vitamins A, D, E, B1, B2, B6, C during physical fatigue, pregnancy/lactation, reduced stamina during or after illness, growth periods, and old age; relief of neuralgia, muscle pain, joint pain (lower-back pain, stiff shoulders, etc.); relief of beriberi, eye fatigue, angular cheilitis, cheilitis, stomatitis, glossitis, eczema, and dermatitis; and prevention of poor bone and tooth development and rickets.
576a17b04fc3ca8f.usage:
Children aged 12 and older and adults: take 1–2 tablets once daily after a meal.
Follow the prescribed dosage.
576a17b04fc3ca8f.caution:
Warning: Taking 5,000 IU or more of vitamin A per day may cause congenital malformations. Women within the first 3 months of pregnancy or who may be pregnant should not take this medicine. Overdose in children aged 6 or under may cause fatal iron poisoning, so store out of the reach of children.

Do not take this medicine if any of the following applies: hypercalcemia; sarcoidosis; kidney disease; those hypersensitive to this medicine; infants under 12 months; Wilson's disease; hemochromatosis; hemosiderosis; non-iron-deficiency anemia; kidney stones; severe renal failure; hereditary problems such as galactose intolerance, Lapp lactase deficiency, or glucose-galactose malabsorption; or those hypersensitive to Yellow No. 5.

Consult a pharmacist before use if you have hyperoxaluria; are pregnant, may be pregnant, or are breastfeeding; premature infants, infants; gastrointestinal disorders such as peptic ulcer, chronic ulcerative colitis, or regional enteritis; cardiac/circulatory dysfunction; renal impairment; hypoproteinemia; are being treated with cardiac glycosides; gallbladder-related disease; liver disease; diabetes; gout; kidney stones or a history of them; are deficient in folic acid; or have a thrombotic predisposition.

Follow the prescribed dosage and usage.

This medicine may turn urine yellow, affecting clinical test values, and may interfere with the detection of blood glucose in urine tests.

While taking this medicine, do not take phosphates, calcium salts, oral tetracyclines, antacids, or levodopa. Consult a pharmacist when taking with cardiac glycosides, estrogen-containing oral contraceptives, antialdosterone agents, or triamterene. Avoid tannin-containing teas such as green tea and black tea during, before, and after taking this medicine.

If nausea, vomiting, itching, dry and rough skin, painful joint swelling, diarrhea, gastric discomfort, constipation, rash, redness, loose stools, stomatitis, low blood pressure, facial flushing, irregular heartbeat, skin rash, hives, photosensitivity, abdominal/stomach pain, cramps, fever, coma, upper abdominal pain, red spots, cardiac arrest, central nervous system depression, dermatitis, body odor in sweat/breath, hair loss, restlessness, gastrointestinal disorders, indigestion, pulmonary edema, or menstruation coming earlier than expected, increasing in amount, or bleeding for a prolonged period occur, stop immediately and consult a pharmacist.

summaryTable.How it works: Supplies vitamins A, D, E, B-group and C for fatigue, recovery, growth and old age
summaryTable.Main symptoms: Physical fatigue, neuralgia/muscle/joint pain, beriberi, stomatitis, eczema, dermatitis
